      <content name="title">Myositis</content>

      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt0">Dermatomyositis</span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Polymyositis</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Myositis means inflammation of the muscles that you use to move your body. An injury, infection, or autoimmune disease can cause it. Two specific kinds are polymyositis and <span class="qt0">dermatomyositis</span>. Polymyositis causes muscle weakness, usually in the muscles closest to the trunk of your body. <span class="qt0">Dermatomyositis</span> causes muscle weakness, plus a skin rash.</p><p>Other symptoms of myositis may include:</p><ul><li>Fatigue after walking or standing</li><li>Tripping or falling</li><li>Trouble swallowing or breathing</li></ul><p>Doctors may use a physical exam, lab tests, imaging tests and a muscle biopsy to diagnose myositis. There is no cure for these diseases, but you can treat the symptoms. Polymyositis and <span class="qt0">dermatomyositis</span> are first treated with high doses of a corticosteroid. Other options include medications, physical therapy, exercise, heat therapy, assistive devices, and rest.</p><p>NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke</p></content>
